paragraphs.source_en: One afternoon, I went out to the veranda as usual for a nap and had a delightful dream in which I had become a tiger. In the dream I ordered my master, "Bring me chicken!" My master hastily answered and at once brought the chicken with trembling care. Just then Meitei also arrived, and I said to him, "I want to eat wild goose. Go to the goose-hotpot shop and buy me a portion!" As usual, Meitei replied in his reckless joking tone, "If you eat it together with pickled turnip and salted rice crackers, the goose will taste even better." I opened my great mouth and let out a low "grr" to frighten him. Meitei instantly turned pale and hurriedly said, "The goose-hotpot shop down the hill has gone out of business. What shall I do?" I said, "In that case I shall make do with beef. Hurry to Nishikawa's and buy me a cut of sirloin! If you are not quick, I shall eat you first!" At that, Meitei promptly tucked up his long robe and ran out. Since my body had suddenly grown enormous, I lay there filling the whole veranda. I was waiting for Meitei to return when suddenly a great sound rang through the entire house; startled, I woke from the dream before I could eat that precious beef. At that moment the master, who only a moment before had been trembling and bowing meekly before me, was completely transformed. He suddenly sprang out of the privy and stamped hard on my stomach. Greatly puzzled, I saw him thrust his feet into the garden clogs, turn around by the side gate, and dash off toward Rakuunkan. Having just shrunk from the tiger of my dream back into a cat, I myself felt rather ridiculous and somewhat embarrassed. But because of my master's terrifying fury and the painful blow to my belly, I immediately forgot the splendid dream of having become a tiger. Enduring the pain, I thought, "Now that the master himself has taken the field, there should be something worth seeing!" So I followed close behind my master and went out to the back gate. I heard my master roar, "Thief!" There I saw a very sturdy youth of eighteen or nineteen, wearing a school cap, climbing over the lattice fence to the other side. I thought, "Ah, too late." The young fellow took up a running posture and fled for his life. Seeing that his cry of "Thief" had produced a great effect, my master again shouted loudly, "Thief! Thief!" and ran after him. But in order to catch up with the enemy, my master would have to leap over this fence. Yet if my master penetrated deep into the enemy's territory, he himself would become a thief. As I have said before, my master is a famous hothead. Since he had so impetuously set off in pursuit of the thief, it seemed he had resolved to chase him to the end, even if he himself became a thief. Thus he advanced all the way to the base of the fence, with no sign whatever of turning back. At the critical instant when one more step would have brought him into the thief's domain, an officer from the enemy army, sporting a sparse little mustache, came leisurely forward. He and my master were talking about something across the fence. When I listened closely, I found that they were conducting a perfectly pointless negotiation.

paragraphs.source_zh: 一天下午，我照例到廊前午睡，做了一个自己变成了老虎的美梦。在梦中我命令主人说：“拿鸡肉来！”主人赶忙答应，立刻小心翼翼地拿来了鸡肉。这时迷亭也来了，我对迷亭说：“我想吃大雁，你到雁锅铺去，给我买一份来！”迷亭照例还是用那种胡乱开玩笑的口吻说：“您要是和腌芜菁、椒盐饼一齐吃，那大雁就更有味道啦。”我张开大口，发出“哼”的一声来威吓他。迷亭脸色立刻变得苍白，赶忙说：“山下的雁锅铺已经歇业了，怎么办呢？”我说：“要是那样，我对付着吃牛肉吧，你赶快到西川铺去给我买一片牛里脊来！不快些，我就先把你吃了！”于是迷亭连忙拉起长袍跑了出去。我由于身体突然变大，在廊子里躺着，将廊子塞得满满的。我等待迷亭回来，忽然整栋房子发出了一个很大的声响，我被吓得没吃成那十分难得的牛肉就从梦中醒来了。这时，刚才还战战兢兢在我面前低首下心的主人，此刻完全变了个样。他猛地从茅房里跳出来，狠狠地踩了我的肚子一脚。我大为奇怪，只见他拖上到院子里用的木屐，转过旁门，向落云馆方向飞跑而去。我刚刚从梦中的老虎变回到猫儿上来，自己也觉得怪滑稽的，有些不好意思。但由于主人这一吓人的气势和肚子挨了他怪痛的一脚，我立刻忘掉了刚才变成老虎的美梦。我强忍着疼痛，心想：“这回主人亲自出马了，有好戏看啦！”于是我紧跟在主人身后来到了后门。我听见主人一声大喝：“小偷！”只见一个十八九岁的、非常健壮的戴着制帽的小伙子，正在从方格的篱笆向外跨越。我想：“啊呀，太晚了。”只见那小伙子采取跑步的姿势，不顾命地飞跑着。主人看到自己喊的这声“小偷”很奏效，便又高声喊着“小偷！小偷！”追了上去。但是为了追上敌人，主人不得不从这墙跳过去。可是主人如果深入对方的重地，自己可就成了小偷啦。前边已经说过，主人是个有名的虚火上升者。他既然这样一鼓作气地追赶小偷，看起来是已经下了决心，即使自己变为小偷也要猛追到底。于是他一直追到了墙根，还毫无折回的样子。就在这再进一步他就踩入了小偷领域的千钧一发之际，敌军当中有一位留着一撮小胡子的将官不慌不忙地出马了。他与主人隔着篱笆在谈着什么。我仔细一听，原来他们在进行毫无意义的谈判。

paragraphs.source_en: I had expected this negotiation to produce the magnificent spectacle of dragons rising and tigers battling, yet to my surprise it ended safely in this prosaic exchange. My master's vigor shows only in the force of his onset; when the crucial moment comes, it always ends in this anticlimax, just as I had suddenly returned from my tiger dream to the reality of being a cat. This is the minor incident to which I referred. Having finished recounting this small affair, in proper order of development I must of course tell of the great affair.

paragraphs.source_en: My master lay prone in the parlor by the paper door leading to the veranda, pondering something. Most likely he was considering what defensive strategy to adopt against the enemy. Rakuunkan seemed to be in class; the athletic field was unusually quiet, and only the voice of a teacher lecturing on ethics in one classroom of the school building could be heard distinctly, clear, resonant, and quite pleasing. Listening closely, I realized that the lecturer was none other than the "general" who had personally come forth from the enemy side yesterday to handle the negotiations.
